text:
Andrea (CS): FYI - escalated from @customer: they see duplicate completions after an SSE reconnect. Customer says they were billed twice for the same generation. sending logs and repro steps below.

Maya (Support): customer reported partial output before disconnect, then on reconnect they got the rest + a duplicate finish token.

Andrea (CS): Repro notes from customer: 1) open streaming session to /v1/streams with model=redwood-large 2) get partial text, then network blips, client reconnects using last_event_id from SSE 3) server returns events that repeat the final chunk and emits a second finalization event -> duplicate generation.

Customer snippet (copied):
```bash
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "X-Request-ID: 0b9f7a" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-large&stream=true"
```

Customer logs (truncated):
```
time=2026-02-18T14:20:11Z level=info msg="stream:start" req_id=0b9f7a client_ip=1.2.3.4
time=2026-02-18T14:20:12Z level=info msg="sse:event" seq=1 req_id=0b9f7a data_len=512
time=2026-02-18T14:20:13Z level=warning msg="connection lost" req_id=0b9f7a
time=2026-02-18T14:20:14Z level=info msg="resume request" last_event_id=1 req_id=0b9f7a
time=2026-02-18T14:20:15Z level=info msg="sse:event" seq=1 req_id=0b9f7a data_len=512
time=2026-02-18T14:20:15Z level=info msg="sse:event" seq=2 req_id=0b9f7a data_len=128
```

Sam (Billing): If the customer was billed twice we need the two request ids / charge ids. Sam: can you pull charge logs for req_id 0b9f7a for the window 14:20:00-14:21:00?

Kevin (eng-runtime): thanks for the repro. initial guess: resume semantics are handing off to a fresh generation when resume token mismatch or when idempotency header is missing. server seems to re-emit seq=1 after resume which suggests we re-stream from the beginning of cached chunks rather than acking the client offset. That can look like a duplicate generation if client treats finalization as a separate completion.

Lucy (eng-ml): also possible: tokenization boundary - finalization event is emitted twice if the model produced the EOS and then resumed and we re-run the last step. Need to check KV cache resume logic + canary for quantized kernels.

Maya (Support): Customer mentioned they do set X-Request-ID but do not include an idempotency key. They rely on SSE Last-Event-ID header.

Andrea (CS): customer asks for short-term mitigations (they're in prod).

Kevin (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigations we can propose to customer: 1) client-side dedupe based on SSE event id: ignore any event with id <= last_processed_id; 2) include an explicit header X-Idempotency-Key on the original request and reuse the same key on reconnect attempts so server can detect resume vs new generation; 3) if available, use our `?resume=true&last_event_id=<id>` query param to force resume semantics.

Andrea (CS): can you give a sample curl for last-event-id resume?

Kevin (eng-runtime): sure - example:
```bash
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  -H "Last-Event-ID: 1" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: abc-123" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-large&stream=true&resume=true"
```

Kevin (eng-runtime): server should respond with `id: 2` for next event, not re-emit 1. If we see seq collisions we need to trace resume token mapping.

Lucy (eng-ml): For longer-term fix: we should ensure the runtime honors idempotency-key at resume and that resume uses cache offset rather than replaying the whole chunk. Also add a server-sent `id:` field with monotonically increasing generation seq and make dedupe idempotent across backend restarts.

Maya (Support): Customer also worried about partial outputs + repeated finalization causing UI weirdness. Suggest we recommend client: show partial outputs as provisional and only credit/bill on `event: completion` with `status: finalized` field.

Sam (Billing): I'll hold refunds until we confirm duplicate charge. if there are two charge ids we can refund one; otherwise we may need to issue one-off credit and follow up.

Kevin (eng-runtime): next steps for eng-runtime: 1) check resume handling for streams around 14:20:14-15 on the node that served req_id 0b9f7a. 2) search logs for `resume request` paired with `sse:event seq=1` pattern. 3) add temporary server-side dedupe: if resume header present and X-Idempotency-Key absent, prefer cache resume instead of full regen.

Lucy (eng-ml): I'll add a unit test against the kv-cache resume semantics and a small integration test that simulates a reconnect at random token boundaries to assert no duplicate `completion` events.

Maya (Support): Reply to customer with repro guidance and mitigation steps above. Also ask for the two request ids / response headers that contain server-charge-id.

Andrea (CS): assigning to @Kevin (eng-runtime) and @Lucy (eng-ml) to investigate; cc @Sam (Billing) for possible refund. please update this thread with findings. :pray:

deploy-bot: scheduled job `stream-resume-trace` started for req_id=0b9f7a (will capture 2m of detailed trace).

Kevin (eng-runtime): started trace capture. I can see a node restart within the 30s window that may have evicted the in-memory resume mapping — that could explain fallback to replay. digging deeper.

Kevin (eng-runtime): preliminary root cause: a short-lived restart cleared ephemeral resume state; server falls back to replaying from chunk 0 and re-emits seq=1. behavior triggers duplicate finalization events because client treats the two finalization signals as two completions.

Lucy (eng-ml): workaround implemented on canary: persist resume offsets to local disk so restart won't drop offsets; rolling this to more nodes. also pushing a change to mark `completion` events with a generation-id that is dedupe-keyed to idempotency keys + resume-offset.

Sam (Billing): found two charge entries: charge_01F... and charge_01F... (same amount) for req_id=0b9f7a and duplicate generated id uuid-dup. issuing a refund for the duplicate now and notifying the customer.

Andrea (CS): customer notified, refund issued, sent mitigation steps, and asked them to test with X-Idempotency-Key + Last-Event-ID.

Kevin (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) instrument server to log resume_mode=(persistent|ephemeral) + resume_key when we see a resume. 2) ensure default behavior is to prefer resume-offset where available, and only replay if resume offset not found AND idempotency-key not present.

Lucy (eng-ml): we'll add the integration test and schedule a small perf run to validate disk-backed offsets don't regress latency significantly.

Andrea (CS): closure? customer confirmed they tested with idempotency + last-event-id and no duplicates observed. closing once canary changes deploy to prod.

Maya (Support): thanks team :thumbsup:
